entries.title: Local-first answering
questions: Does Askwise need Gemini to answer?
Can it work if the AI service is offline?
entries.answer: Askwise searches your saved knowledge base first. It can answer known questions without Gemini. Gemini is only used when the local information is not a confident match or you ask for deeper explanation. If Gemini is unavailable, Askwise still uses local information and tells you when it cannot verify an answer.

entries.title: Importing a knowledge base
questions: How do I add my own knowledge?
What file format can I import?
entries.answer: Open Knowledge Base and choose Import JSON. Askwise accepts a JSON object with an `entries` array or a JSON array of entries. Each entry needs a title and answer; keywords, category, relatedTerms, questions, source, and notes are optional. Imported content is saved in this browser profile. Use Export JSON to back it up or move it to another browser.

entries.title: Where imported knowledge is stored
questions: Is my knowledge uploaded to a server?
Will my notes appear on another device?
Can I back up imported data?
entries.answer: Imported knowledge is stored in this browser's local storage and is not uploaded just by importing it. It does not automatically sync to other devices or browser profiles. Export the knowledge base as JSON to keep a backup or move it. When you explicitly use Gemini, only a few relevant excerpts are sent to Gemini with the question and recent conversation context.

entries.title: Answer sources and confidence
questions: How do I know where an answer came from?
What if it does not know?
entries.answer: A local answer shows the knowledge-base entries that support it. Askwise does not treat a weak match as verified; it can ask Gemini for additional help or say the available sources are insufficient. Gemini is instructed to preserve the local sources and not invent or contradict facts as though they came from your knowledge base.

entries.title: Conversation context and follow-up questions
questions: Does Askwise remember what I just asked?
Can I ask a follow-up without repeating the subject?
How does it know what 'that' means?
entries.answer: Askwise keeps the current chat in the browser and uses recent turns to interpret follow-ups. If you ask “what about that?” or “tell me more,” it carries the current subject into the next search or Gemini request. Starting a new chat clears that conversation context.

entries.title: Gemini API configuration
questions: Where do I put my Gemini key?
Why does Gemini mode say it needs a key?
Can the browser read the secret?
entries.answer: For local development, copy `.env.example` to `.env` in the project root and set `GEMINI_API_KEY` there. The Express server reads the key; React never receives it. In a managed deployment, configure the secret in the server environment. If the key is missing, Askwise continues to answer from local knowledge and explains that Gemini assistance is not configured.
